items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: named George Shaw, who played trombone, banjo. He had an expert banjoist from Chicago named Connie Webster. And actually, Connie wasn't with this Crawford group I played with. He was with another group. But I believe that about covers the men in the band when I joined.

ctx.x: Yeah. Always had good musicians. Uh, back to Hamm Crawford, we have mentioned some of the people with him. Uh huh. But, uh, could you name some of the people that were in the band when you were with him?

Yeah, I sure can, and some who were with him later who were remarkably good musicians. When I joined Hamm, he had a pianist named Eddie Whitley. He had, uh, a drummer named Buddy Seaman. And this Buddy Seaman was the Buddy of the Buddy's Blue Melody Boys, which was organized later, from a Hamm Crawford band. And he had a, uh, a guy named Harry Mullins on banjo. And a guy from St. Louis named George Shaw, who played trombone, banjo. He had an expert banjoist from Chicago named Connie Webster. And actually, Connie…

I know somebody who still makes. Is that right? She occasionally does it for, you know, a social organization. She makes them for the New Leviathan Oriental Foxtrot Orchestra. I don't know if you've heard them or not. I've told you about them.
